question: Why is a radioactive atom more dangerous than its radiation at a distance?
answer: Radiation from a source falls off fast with distance, and much of it can't even get through air; a little material blocks it. A radioactive atom you breathe in sits right beside your cells and fires its radiation straight into them, so it can't miss.
move: Radiation far away fades; a radioactive atom inside you hits cells directly.
